goal: Stop spending GitHub Actions minutes on private repos: run their CI on the Mac and report the result on the PR. Jobs that stay on Actions default to GitHub, with a local fallback when GitHub doesn't start them.
changed: New bstack skill local-ci: local_ci.py runs a repo's scripts/ci at a commit in a throwaway worktree and posts the `local-ci` commit status; a red run on a PR leaves one comment with the end of the log.
install sets up a launchd agent that ticks every five minutes over open PR heads and the default branch head, skipping any sha with a finished status and rerunning a stale pending one.

fallback runs scripts/fallback/<job> from the base branch for each Actions job GitHub finished without starting, against the PR's merge commit, and posts `<job> (local fallback)`; jobs that ran on GitHub are never replaced and `# local-ci: explicit` scripts run only by name.

claims.claim: Pass, fail with one edited comment, run's exit code following an existing verdict and waiting for a running tick, finished vs stale pending, missing scripts/ci, timeout, moved head, fork PRs, --force and an untouched clone behave as the SKILL.md says. fallback: refused jobs run the base branch's script on the merge commit while the PR's own copy never runs; jobs that ran on GitHub are left alone; explicit scripts need --job; a stale merge ref, a missing script, a failing checker and --dry-run behave as documented.
claims.check: tests/test_local_ci.py, 22 end-to-end tests against a real bare repo and a stub gh; eight mutants each turn one test red
claims.remaining: The stub gh, not GitHub. macOS only for install.

claims.claim: Against real GitHub, run --pr posts success on a passing PR and failure plus a comment naming the broken file on a failing one, and the installed launchd agent's first tick gave every open PR head and default branch head a verdict.
claims.check: four private-repo PRs and one throwaway PR with a planted formatting error, statuses read back with gh api; local_ci.py status after the first tick
claims.remaining: The repos are private, so the statuses are not linked here. Only one machine has run it.

claims.claim: Against real GitHub, fallback classified billing-refused ledger jobs as not started and a deploy that ran as started, then ran three repos' ledger fallbacks on their PRs' merge commits and posted success; the ledger fallback fails on a tampered ledger.
claims.check: local_ci.py fallback --pr on three private-repo PRs with --checker-ref the PR branch (the script was not on main yet); the fallback script on a local commit editing a sealed ledger line, exit 1
claims.remaining: The repos are private, so the statuses are not linked here. The first runs took the script from the PR branch, not the base.

next.item: Book local runs' test records in the quality books
next.why_now: Repos that move to local-ci stop producing the Actions artifacts that quality.py fetch reads.
next.impact: Until then those repos' per-test time and flakes drop out of the weekly brief.
